prompt:
Return one bare JSON object with exactly these keys: name, phone, email, company, country. Each value must be a string or JSON null. Do not output Markdown or commentary.

1. Extract only the label/value lines in the single contact block. Labels and line order vary; separators include colon, equals and tab. Never use surrounding notes, signatures, email domains or company suffixes to supply values. Trim each value and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent lines, empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing fields are null except for the country inference in step 3.

2. Assign values before formatting. Reserve the country line for country. Among other nonmissing values, assign any value containing @ to email regardless of label. Assign a value to phone regardless of label if, after removing a leading tel: and a trailing extension (ext., ext, x, # or extension followed by digits), it has at least seven digits and contains only digits, spaces and + - ( ) . /. For name and company, use their labeled values, but swap them if the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not. Check for the suffix before removing it. Legal suffixes, matched case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

3. Resolve country and phone together. Normalize a nonmissing country-line value to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish or German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases, all case-insensitively. Map UK and Great Britain to GB, Holland to NL, USA and U.S.A. to US, Türkiye to TR, and Czech Republic to CZ. To format a phone, first drop tel: and the extension. After ignoring an initial opening parenthesis, a leading + or 00 marks an international number. For an international number, remove (0) and all spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and replace initial 00 with +. Keep its written calling code even if the country line disagrees. If the country is missing, fill it from the international calling code only if that code belongs to exactly one country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For a national number, strip the same separators, remove exactly one leading trunk 0 if present, and prepend + and the normalized country's calling code. If there is no country, a national phone is null. Every non-null phone is E.164: + followed only by digits.

4. Format the remaining fields. For name, reorder Last, First at the first comma, drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof, case-insensitively and with an optional dot, and uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. For company, strip one trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. For email, remove enclosing angle brackets and a mailto: prefix, including when the prefix is inside the brackets, then lowercase the entire address. Trim and collapse whitespace in the final values.
